title: Sprint stitch: security sketch & evidence ops (personal)
content:
Brain dump (two-week sprint mentality)

Purpose: collect quick actionable items, things to hand off, and evidence naming rules for audit folder build. This is a messy personal scratchpad — will tidy into a checklist/matrix next.

TOPLINE NOTES
- Focus areas for next 10 working days: key management + rotation, prod sys access reviews, log retention verification, control owners, basic evidence artifacts for read-only customer/private deployments.
- Goal: ship an evidence folder prototype for one control set (CC6/Access Controls and CC7/System Operations) and iterate.

QUICK QUESTIONS (unresolved)
- Legal: retention minimum for infra logs for customers in EU? (ask Marta) -> action: ping legal slack @marta, copy compliance owner
- Do we have a canonical artifact for "key rotation performed" for KMS in Dedicated vs Private deploy? Currently: KMS rotation policy docs + rotation events in audit logs. Is that sufficient?
- Is Cloud HSM onboarding in scope for Private for SOC2 now or deferred? (depends on sales commitments)

EVIDENCE NAMING CONVENTION (proposal)
- {control-id}_{env}_{artifact-type}_{date}_{ownerInitials}.pdf OR .log
- example: CC6_prod_access-review_2026-03-09_LS.pdf
- Keep short but searchable; must match entries in control-mapping spreadsheet (id column).

CONTROL MAPPING (sketch)
- CC6 (Access) -> artifacts: access-review spreadsheet, IAM policy snapshots, SRE ticket for emergency access, onboarding/offboarding checklist
- CC7 (Ops) -> artifacts: runbooks, change-history (git PRs), deployment audit logs, incident postmortems
- CC8 (Data protection) -> artifacts: KMS policy doc, encryption-at-rest config, key rotation logs, storage ACL snapshots

SIMPLE MINI-PROJECT: "Access review pipeline"
- Steps:
  1) Export active service accounts + human users from IAM tool (script exists: infra/scripts/export-iam.py) -> output csv in /evidence/temp
  2) Annotate each account with owner and purpose (manual: ask team leads)
  3) Create ticket template for access removal/justification (Jira SEC-AC-REV template)
  4) Save snapshot as: CC6_prod_access-review_2026-03-12_KS.csv and commit to evidence-sandbox (read-only path)
- Blockers: we need accurate owner mapping; SRE has partial mapping in their internal doc. Action: pair w/ Omar for 90m to reconcile.

KEY MANAGEMENT (notes)
- Two tracks: Hosted (Redwood-managed KMS) and Private (customer KMS or customer-managed keys).
- Evidence items we can pull quickly: KMS rotation policy (doc), Cloud KMS logs (rotation events), IAM bindings to key rings, PR that changed rotation policy (git history).
- Quick checklist for proof: policy doc + rotation event log within last 12 months + PR/approval record.

LOGS + RETENTION
- Need to validate: retention policy config for token-level logs, request traces, and infra metrics. Where stored? Long-term logs in GCS with lifecycle policy.
- Verify lifecycle rule: log-archive-bkt -> 400 days? (looks like 400 in one bucket, 90 in another). Confirm with infra.
- Action: script to sample bucket lifecycle config and list objects older than retention threshold. Put results into evidence snapshot.

ACCESS REVIEWS & ORPHANED KEYS
- Quick scan for orphaned credentials: rotate or delete anything with owner "svc-unknown" or with no owner tag.
- Suggestion: automate weekly report; for now, manual triage for top 10 by privileges.

TODAY'S TODOS (short)
- [ ] Create CC6 sample evidence folder (prod) with 3 artifacts (access csv, policy snapshot, Jira ticket). (Owner: Kiran)
- [ ] Sync w/ Omar (30–60m) to reconcile owner map for 8 service accounts. (Owner: Kiran/Omar)
- [ ] Ping Marta for retention policy clarification (Owner: Kiran)
- [ ] Draft KMS rotation evidence template and circulate (Owner: Lena)

HANDOFF NOTES FOR SRE (what I will hand off after sprint)
- Minimal artifact set for each control: 1) policy doc, 2) activity log extract (timestamped), 3) change record (PR/ticket). If any one of these is missing, mark control "incomplete" and list remediation steps.
- For Private deployments: include customer-provided key ownership proof (customer confirmation email or signed SOC2 addendum).

COMMUNICATION / SLACK PING TEMPLATE (quick)
- "Heads up: running access review for prod service accounts this week. If you're listed as owner of an account but it's no longer used, please reply or mark in the spreadsheet by EOD Thursday. Contact @Omar for questions"

RISKS / HOT PATHS
- Risk: evidence mismatch — audit team asks for a particular date but logs rotated out. Mitigation: keep a minimal long-term archive (s3/gcs) for audit artifacts and export daily digest of changes for critical controls.
- Risk: private deploys with customer KMS lack central audit — need signed attestation or automated audit-forwarding.

NOTES FROM PAIRING WITH LENA (3/9)
- Lena suggests: prioritize controls that have customer-visible impact (access, encryption). She has a template to convert runbooks into evidence.
- She proposed a "control owner" tag in PR descriptions to speed mapping. Could be enforced as a pre-commit hook in infra repos.

NEXT STEPS (end of sprint)
- Consolidate example evidence docs and submit a short readme that maps each artifact to control ID and the verifier's expected proof.
- Convert this scratch into a proper playbook under confluence: /SOC2/Evidence-Playbooks/Access-Review (owner: Kiran).

RANDOM TODOs (low priority)
- Inventory: list of repos with infra IAM changes in last 24 months
- Cleanup: stale service accounts older than 18 months with no activity
- Automate snapshot exports for evidence weekly (cron job)

SIGNOFF (personal reminder)
- Keep iterations small. If legal needs a different artifact format, pivot quickly. The goal this sprint is consistency and reproducibility more than completeness.

----
End of scratchpad. Will prune and produce a tidy checklist file for sharing with Lena and Omar by Fri 2026-03-13.
